mechanism_narrative: Sustained low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) reduce equity discount rates and increase capital allocation to stocks, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as valuation multiples expand.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.1% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate falling below 5.0% signals labor market tightening, accelerating consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST > 950k) and retail sales (RSAFS > 430k) growth indicate robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST > 950.0 and RSAFS > 430000.0.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing expansion (INDPRO > 100) signals rising industrial output and profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when INDPRO > 100 for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 16000) indicates accelerating economic activity, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >50% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.5% annually.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals potential Fed rate hikes, increasing equity discount rates and reducing valuation multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly) combined with falling unemployment (UNRATE decline > 0.1pp) indicates labor market tightness, triggering wage inflation and Fed rate hikes that reduce equity returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5 and UNRATE decline > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing contraction (INDPRO < 100) signals declining industrial output and profit erosion, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as recession fears increase.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 100 for 3 consecutive months.
